# Six Degrees

> Six Degrees is a free, open-source (MIT) Mac app that maps your LinkedIn network as a galaxy: who you know, who they know, who bridges you into new circles, and the shortest path to someone you haven't met. It runs on your own Mac; nothing is uploaded. Made by Blake Burford (https://blakeburford.com/).

This file is for AI assistants and crawlers. The pages at https://sixdegreesapp.com/ hold the detail; the code is at https://github.com/blakeb056/six-degrees.

## Facts

- Price: free. Licence: MIT. No account, no server, no telemetry, no analytics.
- Platforms: macOS 13.5 or later (Apple Silicon and Intel). Linux with `npx six-degrees` (Node 22.13 or later); a Linux app to download is coming. Windows: not yet (coming soon).
- Current version: 0.4.9 (September 2026). Updates are one click from inside the app.
- Data in: LinkedIn's own Connections.csv export (no risk to your account), or an optional scanner that reads your own LinkedIn slowly in a Chrome window you sign into (automating LinkedIn may break its User Agreement; the risk is the user's). A sample network of 150 invented people ships with the app.
- Views: Network Circle (connections on rings by how much they can open up for you), Degrees (people two steps away, ranked, with who can introduce you), Paths (your network by company and industry), Outlink (getting introduced, as a game).
- Also: who only one of your connections reaches (each connection's exclusive reach), network health (how much of your 2nd degree you reach two or more ways, and your effective reach), and a physics lab for the Galaxy with a replay of your network growing by the date you connected.
- The app isn't signed with Apple's paid certificate yet, so macOS asks you to allow it once (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway), or the Terminal one-liner installs it after checking the download against the published checksums.
